title: Company-wide policies and processes: access, change, data, procurement, vendors, travel, templates
author: Elena Park
content:
Summary
=======
This document centralizes the company-wide policies and standard processes for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and commonly used internal templates. It is intended as the canonical reference for employees, managers, and cross-functional teams.

Scope
-----
Applies to all Redwood Inference employees, contractors, and vendors who access corporate systems, handle company data, request or approve spend, or act as contract owners. Some areas reference more restrictive addenda (e.g., security-restricted teams, regulated customers) — those are called out where applicable.

Contacts
--------
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com (policy steward and travel/benefits)
- Security: security@redwood.com (access reviews, vendor security assessments)
- Finance: finance@redwood.com (procurement, expense policy, POs)
- IT/Infra: infra@redwood.com (device management, corporate accounts)
- Legal: legal@redwood.com (contracts and vendor terms)

1) Access & Permissions (RBAC and SSO)
-----------------------------------
Principles
- Least privilege: grant the minimum access required.
- Role-based access control (RBAC): use predefined roles where possible; avoid permanent individual elevated privileges.
- Centralized identity: all user authentication flows through Okta SSO and SCIM provisioning into downstream systems.

Standard roles and approvals
| Role | Systems | Typical Privileges | Approver |
|---|---|---|---|
| Viewer | Confluence, Dashboards | Read-only | Team Manager |
| Developer | Git, CI/CD, Dev projects | Push/Build, dev env access | Eng Manager + Infra Owner |
| Oncall | Monitoring, PagerDuty | Alerting, runbook access | Eng Manager + SRE Lead |
| Admin | GCP/GHA/Vault | Admin console access | Infra Director + Security |

Access request process (standard)
1. Submit request via the Access Request form (Jira: ACCESS-REQ template).
2. Requestor adds justification, expected duration (temporary/permanent), and selects requested role.
3. Manager review and approval (SLO: 3 business days).
4. Security/Infra approval for elevated scopes (SLO: additional 2 business days).
5. Provisioning performed via automated SCIM or manual Jira-to-Okta ticket; requester notified on completion.

Emergency access (break-glass)
- For immediate operational needs, contact on-call SRE and file an ACCESS-REQ marked 'emergency'. Security team will provision temporary credentials with a maximum duration of 12 hours; an audit ticket must be filed within 24 hours.

Access review cadence
- Quarterly automated access review run by Security. Team managers must confirm or revoke listed accounts within 7 business days.

2) Change Management
--------------------
Objectives: minimize customer impact and service interruption while enabling predictable deployment of infrastructure and application changes.

Change categories
- Standard: pre-authorized low-risk changes (e.g., documentation updates, routine config tweaks). No CCB approval required; apply in maintenance window.
- Normal: requires Change Control Board (CCB) approval. Includes schema migrations, infra changes, release to production.
- Emergency: unplanned high-impact changes (incident mitigations). Follow emergency change process and post-facto CCB review.

Change request workflow
1. Create a Change Request (Jira: CHANGE-REQ) with impact assessment, rollback plan, and test plan.
2. Attach deployment playbook, owner, and scheduled maintenance window (if applicable).
3. CCB review: weekly triage meetings for normal changes; approvals logged in Jira (SLO: 5 business days for approval cycle).
4. Execute change during approved window; monitor metrics and rollback if thresholds exceeded.
5. Post-change review within 3 business days summarizing outcome, incidents, and lessons learned.

Change checklist (must be attached to every normal change)
- Impact statement (customers affected)
- Backout/rollback steps with estimated time-to-restore
- Monitoring/alerting adjustments pre/post change
- Communication plan (status page/Slack channel)
- Security review (if change touches IAM, encryption, network ACLs)

Rollback template (example)
1. Stop the deployment job.
2. Re-deploy last known good artifact (tag: stable-YYYYMMDD).
3. Clear incremental db migrations (if reversible) or run compensating transactions.
4. Validate smoke tests: /health, /metrics, sample requests.
5. Notify stakeholders and update change ticket.

3) Data Management
------------------
Data classification
- Public: safe to publish (marketing collateral).
- Internal: default for most company docs and telemetry.
- Confidential: customer PII, internal security plans, contracts.
- Restricted: regulated or sensitive customer data; access only by vetted teams under NDA and contractual controls.

Storage & encryption
- All data at rest must be encrypted. Cloud storage uses provider-managed encryption plus application-layer encryption where required. Keys are managed in HashiCorp Vault (access via Vault roles).
- Backups: daily snapshots for databases with 30-day primary retention and 1-year archived retention for business-critical datasets.

Data retention & deletion
- Default retention: logs 90 days (short-term), analytics aggregates 2 years, backups 1 year.
- Legal holds override deletion; data subject requests processed within 30 days by Legal + Security.

Data access requests
- Use the Data Access Request form (Jira: DATA-REQ). Requests must include business justification, dataset, and intended use. Security and Data Stewards approve (SLO: 5 business days).

Audit & monitoring
- Access to confidential/restricted datasets is logged and reviewed monthly. Suspicious usage triggers immediate investigation.

4) Procurement & Expenses
-------------------------
Procurement thresholds and approvals
- <$1,000: individual contributor may approve (manager informed).
- $1,000 - $10,000: Manager approval required.
- $10,000 - $50,000: Department head + Finance approval.
- > $50,000: VP-level + Finance + Legal involvement; PO required.

Preferred procurement flow
1. Initiator creates Purchase Request (PR) in Procurement system with vendor, justification, and budget code.
2. Manager-level approval -> Finance verification -> PO generation.
3. Vendor engagement and contract review if > $10k or if third-party will access data/systems.

Corporate card & expense reimbursement
- Cardholders must complete training and use corporate cards for approved travel and vendor subscriptions.
- Expense reports due within 14 days of travel/expense. Receipts required for all items > $25.
- Per-diem and allowable items documented in Travel section below.

Payment & invoice processing
- Invoices submitted to finance@redwood.com. Standard payment terms are Net 30. For expedited requests, contact treasury@redwood.com.

5) Vendor Management
--------------------
Vendor selection & onboarding checklist
1. Business owner submits Vendor Request (Jira: VENDOR-REQ) with scope and data access needs.
2. Procurement and Legal perform commercial review.
3. Security completes vendor risk assessment (SIG or standard questionnaire).
4. Exec sponsor signs off for strategic vendors (> $50k annual).
5. Contract executed and added to vendor registry (owner: Procurement).

Security requirements
- All vendors processing customer or confidential data must complete a security questionnaire and provide evidence (SOC2 report, ISO27001, or equivalent).
- Where vendor manages keys or stores restricted data, require customer-specific encryption and contractual controls.

Periodic review
- Strategic vendors reviewed quarterly; operational vendors reviewed annually. Reviews cover SLAs, security posture, invoices, and relationship health.

Termination & offboarding
- Ensure data return or verified deletion per contract. Revoke all vendor credentials and remove from federated SSO. Generate offboarding checklist in Vendor registry.

6) Travel Policy (overview)
---------------------------
Booking & approvals
- All travel booked through the company travel portal (Concur) where available. International travel requires pre-approval from manager and People Ops at least 10 business days prior.

Allowances & expense rules
- Air: economy for flights under 6 hours; premium economy may be approved for flights > 6 hours or for medical reasons.
- Hotel: mid-tier business hotels; use company-negotiated rates where available.
- Meals: per-diem capped at $75/day domestic, $120/day international unless local policy differs.
- Ground transport: use rideshare or corporate car as appropriate. Receipts required for all claims.

Health & safety
- For travel to restricted or high-risk regions, Security will provide guidance and a trip risk assessment. Employees must complete travel safety training for high-risk travel.

Expense submission
- Submit expenses within 14 days via Concur with receipts attached. Finance will process reimbursements on the next payroll cycle following approval.

7) Internal Templates & Examples
--------------------------------
Quick links to templates (Jira/Confluence templates):
- Access Request (Jira: ACCESS-REQ)
- Change Request (Jira: CHANGE-REQ)
- Data Access Request (Jira: DATA-REQ)
- Vendor Onboarding (Jira: VENDOR-REQ)
- Purchase Request / PO template (Procurement system)
- Travel request & expense report (Concur templates)

Example: Access Request minimal payload (for automation)
{
  "requester": "name@redwood.com",
  "system": "gcp-project:analytics",
  "role": "viewer",
  "duration": "30d",
  "justification": "Access required for Q4 analysis and dashboarding"
}

Policies: enforcement & exceptions
- Exceptions to these policies require documented approval from the policy owner (People Ops) and acceptance by the appropriate risk owner (Security or Finance). Exceptions are recorded and reviewed quarterly.

Governance & review cadence
- People Ops maintains this document and will review major sections annually or sooner after material incidents/regulatory changes. Security, Finance, Legal, and representative engineering teams will participate in scheduled reviews.

Appendix: Useful links
- Identity & Access Guide: /confluence/eng-infra/identity-and-access
- Change Management board: /jira/boards/CHANGE-REQ
- Vendor Registry: /confluence/finance/vendor-registry
